narrative: The tech world sees continued aggressive expansion in Artificial Intelligence, with massive investments in AI startups and infrastructure deals, alongside new AI features from major platforms like YouTube and Meta. However, the rapid pace also raises concerns about privacy with new surveillance methods and significant data breaches, while the space sector pushes forward with new NASA missions and tackles challenges in private launches.

highlights.title: AI coding startup Cognition raises $1B at $25B pre-money valuation
highlights.whyItMatters: This represents a significant venture capital investment and soaring valuation in the rapidly expanding AI sector, highlighting investor confidence.

highlights.title: Nvidia bets $150B on Taiwan as Trump's plan to make US an AI hub backfires
highlights.whyItMatters: Nvidia's substantial investment signals Taiwan's critical role in global AI chip manufacturing and highlights geopolitical influences on tech supply chains.

highlights.title: YouTube to automatically label AI-generated videos
highlights.whyItMatters: This move by a major content platform enhances transparency and helps users differentiate between human-created and AI-generated content, addressing concerns about misinformation.

highlights.title: Websites have a new way to spy on visitors: analyzing their SSD activity
highlights.whyItMatters: This uncovers a novel and concerning method for online tracking, raising new privacy implications for internet users.

highlights.title: UK Visa Portal exposed thousands of applicants’ passports and selfies — then called the lawyers on us
highlights.whyItMatters: A significant data breach affecting sensitive personal information highlights critical cybersecurity vulnerabilities and raises questions about accountability.

highlights.title: NASA’s Webb Reveals Black Hole That Formed Before Its Galaxy
highlights.whyItMatters: This groundbreaking discovery by the Webb telescope challenges fundamental theories about galaxy and black hole formation in the early universe.

highlights.title: Rivian will deliver the first R2 SUVs on June 9
highlights.whyItMatters: This marks a crucial milestone for Rivian with the delivery of its 'most important' model, aiming to broaden its appeal in the competitive EV market.

topics.name: Artificial Intelligence (AI)
topics.summary: AI continues to dominate the tech narrative with massive investments, enterprise adoption, advancements in generative models (music, coding), and efforts toward content transparency (YouTube labeling). It also sparks debates on societal impact and market fit.

topics.name: Space Exploration & Science
topics.summary: NASA leads with new discoveries (early black holes, El Niño monitoring), safety innovations (firefighter sensors), and future mission planning (Artemis III, Landsat 10), while SpaceX faces a Starship booster failure investigation.

topics.name: Consumer Technology
topics.summary: New hardware releases (iPad Air, Motorola Razrs), software updates (Halide app, Spotify features), and changing business models (Roku ads) are driving the user experience, alongside gaming updates and hobbyist tech.

topics.name: Digital Security & Privacy
topics.summary: Concerns over new methods of online tracking, significant data breaches (UK Visa Portal), and coordinated efforts to take down botnets highlight the ongoing battle for digital security and user privacy.

topics.name: Electric Vehicles (EVs)
topics.summary: Key milestones include Rivian's R2 SUV deliveries and the polarizing design of Ferrari's new Luce EV, reflecting the dynamic and competitive nature of the automotive sector, also impacted by international trade policies.

topics.name: Corporate & Business Tech
topics.summary: Major tech companies navigate legal challenges (Tesla lawsuit), evolve business models with new subscriptions (Meta), and achieve significant growth (ClickHouse), alongside platform policy changes from Apple and Google.
